questions.title: Write your own `map`
questions.prompt: Write `map(array, callback)` without using `Array.prototype.map`. Call `callback(item, index, array)` for every item and return a new array of the results. Do not change the original array.

test_cases.name: passes the array
test_cases.call: map([1, 2], (x, i, arr) => arr.length)

test_cases.name: does not use the built-in map
test_cases.call: (() => { const built = Array.prototype.map; Array.prototype.map = () => { throw new Error("used the built-in map"); }; try { return map([1], (n) => n + 1); } finally { Array.prototype.map = built; } })()

questions.title: Write your own `filter`

test_cases.name: nothing matches

test_cases.name: uses truthy values, not just true

test_cases.name: does not use the built-in filter
test_cases.call: (() => { const built = Array.prototype.filter; Array.prototype.filter = () => { throw new Error("used the built-in filter"); }; try { return filter([1, 2], (n) => n > 1); } finally { Array.prototype.filter = built; } })()

questions.title: Write your own `reduce`

test_cases.call: reduce([1, 2, 3], (sum, n) => sum + n, 10)

questions.title: `once(fn)`
questions.prompt: Write `once(fn)`. It returns a new function that calls `fn` only the first time it is called, with the same arguments and `this`. Every later call returns the result of that first call without calling `fn` again.

test_cases.name: calls fn only once
test_cases.call: (() => { let n = 0; const f = once(() => ++n); f(); f(); f(); return n; })()

test_cases.name: returns the first result every time
test_cases.call: (() => { const f = once((x) => x * 2); return [f(2), f(5)]; })()

test_cases.name: fn that returns nothing still runs once
test_cases.call: (() => { let n = 0; const f = once(() => { n++; }); f(); f(); return n; })()

test_cases.name: keeps this

questions.title: `memoize(fn)`

test_cases.name: different arguments run again
test_cases.call: (() => { let calls = 0; const square = memoize((n) => { calls++; return n * n; }); return [square(2), square(3), calls]; })()

test_cases.name: no arguments
test_cases.call: memoize(() => 5)()

test_cases.name: caches falsy results too
test_cases.call: (() => { let calls = 0; const f = memoize(() => { calls++; return 0; }); f(1); f(1); return calls; })()

test_cases.name: 1 and "1" are different arguments
test_cases.call: (() => { const f = memoize((x) => typeof x); return [f(1), f("1")]; })()

questions.title: `debounce(fn, delay)`
questions.prompt: Write `debounce(fn, delay)`. It returns a new function that waits until it has not been called for `delay` ms, then calls `fn` once with the latest arguments and the same `this`. Every new call restarts the wait.

test_cases.name: runs once after a burst of calls
test_cases.call: (async () => { const wait = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); let n = 0; const d = debounce(() => n++, 20); d(); d(); d(); await wait(60); return n; })()

test_cases.name: waits for the delay before running
test_cases.call: (async () => { const wait = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); let n = 0; const d = debounce(() => n++, 50); d(); await wait(10); const before = n; await wait(80); return [before, n]; })()

test_cases.name: uses the latest arguments
test_cases.call: (async () => { const wait = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); let got; const d = debounce((x) => { got = x; }, 20); d(1); d(2); d(3); await wait(60); return got; })()

test_cases.name: each call restarts the wait
test_cases.call: (async () => { const wait = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); let n = 0; const d = debounce(() => n++, 50); d(); await wait(30); d(); await wait(30); const middle = n; await wait(50); return [middle, n]; })()

test_cases.name: separate bursts run separately
test_cases.call: (async () => { const wait = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); let n = 0; const d = debounce(() => n++, 20); d(); await wait(40); d(); await wait(40); return n; })()

test_cases.name: keeps this
test_cases.call: (async () => { const wait = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); let got; const user = { name: "Ann", hi: debounce(function () { got = this.name; }, 10) }; user.hi(); await wait(40); return got; })()

questions.title: `throttle(fn, delay)`
questions.prompt: Write `throttle(fn, delay)`. It returns a new function that calls `fn` right away on the first call, then ignores calls until `delay` ms have passed since the last time `fn` ran. Pass on the arguments and `this`.

test_cases.call: (() => { let n = 0; const t = throttle(() => n++, 50); t(); return n; })()

test_cases.name: runs again after the delay
test_cases.call: (async () => { const wait = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); let n = 0; const t = throttle(() => n++, 50); t(); await wait(70); t(); return n; })()

test_cases.name: passes the arguments
test_cases.call: (() => { let got; const t = throttle((a, b) => { got = a + b; }, 50); t(1, 2); return got; })()

test_cases.name: runs at a steady rate during constant calls

Start them so that at most `limit` run at the same time, starting the next one as soon as one finishes. Resolve with all the results in input order, or reject as soon as any task fails.

test_cases.name: results in input order
test_cases.call: (() => { let running = 0; let max = 0; const task = (ms, v) => async () => { running++; max = Math.max(max, running); await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); running--; return v; }; return runWithLimit([task(30, "a"), task(10, "b"), task(20, "c")], 2); })()

test_cases.name: never more than the limit at once
test_cases.call: (async () => { let running = 0; let max = 0; const task = (ms, v) => async () => { running++; max = Math.max(max, running); await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); running--; return v; }; await runWithLimit([task(20, 1), task(20, 2), task(20, 3), task(20, 4), task(20, 5)], 2); return max; })()

test_cases.name: a limit of 1 runs one at a time
test_cases.call: (async () => { let running = 0; let max = 0; const task = (ms, v) => async () => { running++; max = Math.max(max, running); await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); running--; return v; }; await runWithLimit([task(10, 1), task(10, 2), task(10, 3)], 1); return max; })()

test_cases.name: a limit bigger than the number of tasks
test_cases.call: (() => { let running = 0; let max = 0; const task = (ms, v) => async () => { running++; max = Math.max(max, running); await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); running--; return v; }; return runWithLimit([task(10, 1), task(10, 2)], 5); })()

test_cases.name: empty list
test_cases.call: runWithLimit([], 3)

test_cases.name: runs in parallel up to the limit
test_cases.call: (async () => { let running = 0; let max = 0; const task = (ms, v) => async () => { running++; max = Math.max(max, running); await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); running--; return v; }; const start = Date.now(); await runWithLimit([task(40, 1), task(40, 2), task(40, 3), task(40, 4)], 2); const ms = Date.now() - start; return ms >= 70 && ms < 150; })()

test_cases.name: rejects when a task fails
test_cases.call: runWithLimit([() => Promise.resolve(1), () => Promise.reject(new Error("bad"))], 2).then(() => "resolved", (e) => e.message)

questions.title: `debounce` with `leading`, `trailing` and `cancel`
questions.prompt: Write `debounce(fn, delay, { leading = false, trailing = true } = {})`. With `leading`, call `fn` at the start of a burst of calls. With `trailing`, call it with the latest arguments once calls stop for `delay` ms. With both, a single call runs `fn` only once. Also give the returned function a `cancel()` method that drops any pending call.

test_cases.name: trailing by default
test_cases.call: (async () => { const wait = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); const calls = []; const d = debounce((x) => calls.push(x), 20); d(1); d(2); d(3); await wait(60); return calls; })()

test_cases.name: leading only runs right away, once per burst
test_cases.call: (async () => { const wait = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); const calls = []; const d = debounce((x) => calls.push(x), 20, { leading: true, trailing: false }); d(1); d(2); d(3); const rightAway = [...calls]; await wait(60); return [rightAway, calls]; })()

test_cases.name: leading and trailing run at both ends
test_cases.call: (async () => { const wait = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); const calls = []; const d = debounce((x) => calls.push(x), 20, { leading: true, trailing: true }); d(1); d(2); d(3); await wait(60); return calls; })()

test_cases.name: a single call with leading and trailing runs once
test_cases.call: (async () => { const wait = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); const calls = []; const d = debounce((x) => calls.push(x), 20, { leading: true, trailing: true }); d(1); await wait(60); return calls; })()

test_cases.name: a new burst runs leading again
test_cases.call: (async () => { const wait = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); const calls = []; const d = debounce((x) => calls.push(x), 20, { leading: true, trailing: false }); d(1); await wait(50); d(2); await wait(50); return calls; })()

test_cases.name: cancel drops the pending call
test_cases.call: (async () => { const wait = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); const calls = []; const d = debounce((x) => calls.push(x), 20); d(1); d.cancel(); await wait(50); return calls; })()

test_cases.name: works again after cancel
test_cases.call: (async () => { const wait = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); const calls = []; const d = debounce((x) => calls.push(x), 20); d(1); d.cancel(); d(2); await wait(50); return calls; })()

questions.title: An LRU cache using `Map`
questions.prompt: Write a class `LRUCache` with `constructor(capacity)`, `get(key)` and `put(key, value)`. `get` returns the value, or `-1` if the key is missing, and marks the key as recently used. `put` adds or updates a key and marks it as recently used. When the cache is over capacity, remove the least recently used key. Tip: a `Map` remembers insertion order.

test_cases.name: stores and reads a value
test_cases.call: (() => { const c = new LRUCache(2); c.put("a", 1); return c.get("a"); })()

test_cases.name: a missing key gives -1
test_cases.call: new LRUCache(2).get("x")

test_cases.name: removes the least recently used key
test_cases.call: (() => { const c = new LRUCache(2); c.put("a", 1); c.put("b", 2); c.put("c", 3); return [c.get("a"), c.get("b"), c.get("c")]; })()

test_cases.name: get makes a key recently used
test_cases.call: (() => { const c = new LRUCache(2); c.put("a", 1); c.put("b", 2); c.get("a"); c.put("c", 3); return [c.get("a"), c.get("b")]; })()

test_cases.name: put on an existing key updates it and makes it recent
test_cases.call: (() => { const c = new LRUCache(2); c.put("a", 1); c.put("b", 2); c.put("a", 10); c.put("c", 3); return [c.get("a"), c.get("b"), c.get("c")]; })()

test_cases.name: capacity 1
test_cases.call: (() => { const c = new LRUCache(1); c.put("a", 1); c.put("b", 2); return [c.get("a"), c.get("b")]; })()

test_cases.name: the LeetCode example
test_cases.call: (() => { const c = new LRUCache(2); const out = []; c.put(1, 1); c.put(2, 2); out.push(c.get(1)); c.put(3, 3); out.push(c.get(2)); c.put(4, 4); out.push(c.get(1), c.get(3), c.get(4)); return out; })()

questions.title: A simple `Promise` class
questions.prompt: Write a class `MyPromise` with `constructor(executor)`, `then(onFulfilled, onRejected)` and `catch(onRejected)`, without wrapping the built-in `Promise`. It settles only once. An error thrown in the executor rejects it. `then` returns a new `MyPromise`, runs its callbacks asynchronously, passes on values and errors it has no callback for, and waits for a promise returned by a callback.

test_cases.name: then gets the value
test_cases.call: new MyPromise((resolve) => resolve(5)).then((v) => v * 2)

test_cases.name: chains then calls
test_cases.call: new MyPromise((resolve) => resolve(1)).then((v) => v + 1).then((v) => v * 10)

test_cases.name: catch gets the rejection
test_cases.call: new MyPromise((_, reject) => reject(new Error("no"))).catch((e) => e.message)

test_cases.name: an error thrown in the executor rejects
test_cases.call: new MyPromise(() => { throw new Error("boom"); }).catch((e) => e.message)

test_cases.name: an error in then skips to catch
test_cases.call: new MyPromise((r) => r(1)).then(() => { throw new Error("in then"); }).then(() => "skipped").catch((e) => e.message)

test_cases.name: settles only once
test_cases.call: new MyPromise((resolve, reject) => { resolve(1); resolve(2); reject(new Error("x")); }).then((v) => v, () => "rejected")

test_cases.name: then callbacks run asynchronously
test_cases.call: (async () => { const wait = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); const log = []; new MyPromise((r) => r()).then(() => log.push("then")); log.push("sync"); await wait(10); return log; })()

test_cases.name: waits for a promise returned from then
test_cases.call: new MyPromise((r) => r(1)).then((v) => new MyPromise((r) => setTimeout(() => r(v + 1), 10)))

questions.title: `deepClone` that handles circular references
questions.prompt: Write `deepClone(value)` for plain objects and arrays that also handles circular references, like an object that points to itself. Objects that are shared inside the original must stay shared in the copy. Tip: remember what you have already copied, for example in a `WeakMap`.

test_cases.name: an object that points to itself
test_cases.call: (() => { const a = { name: "a" }; a.self = a; const c = deepClone(a); return [c !== a, c.self === c, c.name]; })()

test_cases.name: two objects that point to each other
test_cases.call: (() => { const a = {}; const b = { a }; a.b = b; const c = deepClone(a); return [c.b.a === c, c.b !== b]; })()

test_cases.name: an array that contains itself
test_cases.call: (() => { const arr = [1]; arr.push(arr); const c = deepClone(arr); return [c[1] === c, c[0], c !== arr]; })()

test_cases.name: shared objects stay shared
test_cases.call: (() => { const shared = { n: 1 }; const o = { x: shared, y: shared }; const c = deepClone(o); return [c.x === c.y, c.x !== shared]; })()

test_cases.name: nested copies are independent
test_cases.call: (() => { const o = { a: { b: 1 } }; const c = deepClone(o); c.a.b = 2; return o.a.b; })()

test_cases.name: primitives and null
test_cases.call: [deepClone(5), deepClone(null), deepClone("s")]

questions.title: `flattenObject(obj)`
questions.prompt: Write `flattenObject(obj)`. Turn nested plain objects into one level, with keys joined by dots: `{ a: { b: 1 } }` becomes `{ "a.b": 1 }`. Arrays and `null` are kept as values, not flattened. An empty nested object adds no keys. Do not change the input.

test_cases.name: one level of nesting
test_cases.call: flattenObject({ a: { b: 1 } })

test_cases.name: empty object
test_cases.call: flattenObject({})

test_cases.name: deep nesting next to a flat key
test_cases.call: flattenObject({ a: { b: { c: { d: 1 } } }, e: 2 })

test_cases.name: an already flat object
test_cases.call: flattenObject({ x: 1, y: "two" })

test_cases.name: arrays are kept as values
test_cases.call: flattenObject({ a: { list: [1, 2] } })

test_cases.name: null is kept as a value
test_cases.call: flattenObject({ a: { b: null } })

test_cases.name: an empty nested object adds no keys
test_cases.call: flattenObject({ a: {}, b: 1 })

test_cases.name: does not change the input
test_cases.call: (() => { const o = { a: { b: 1 } }; flattenObject(o); return o; })()

questions.title: A small `createStore`, like Redux
questions.prompt: Write `createStore(reducer, initialState)`. It returns a store with `getState()`, `dispatch(action)` and `subscribe(listener)`. `dispatch` sets the state to `reducer(state, action)`, calls every listener, and returns the action. `subscribe` returns a function that removes that listener.

test_cases.name: getState returns the initial state
test_cases.call: (() => { const counter = (state, action) => (action.type === "add" ? state + action.by : state); return createStore(counter, 5).getState(); })()

test_cases.name: dispatch updates the state
test_cases.call: (() => { const counter = (state, action) => (action.type === "add" ? state + action.by : state); const store = createStore(counter, 5); store.dispatch({ type: "add", by: 2 }); store.dispatch({ type: "add", by: 2 }); return store.getState(); })()

test_cases.name: an unknown action keeps the state
test_cases.call: (() => { const counter = (state, action) => (action.type === "add" ? state + action.by : state); const store = createStore(counter, 5); store.dispatch({ type: "other" }); return store.getState(); })()

test_cases.name: listeners run after each dispatch and see the new state
test_cases.call: (() => { const counter = (state, action) => (action.type === "add" ? state + action.by : state); const store = createStore(counter, 5); const seen = []; store.subscribe(() => seen.push(store.getState())); store.dispatch({ type: "add", by: 1 }); store.dispatch({ type: "add", by: 2 }); return seen; })()

test_cases.name: unsubscribe stops a listener
test_cases.call: (() => { const counter = (state, action) => (action.type === "add" ? state + action.by : state); const store = createStore(counter, 0); let n = 0; const unsubscribe = store.subscribe(() => n++); store.dispatch({ type: "add", by: 1 }); unsubscribe(); store.dispatch({ type: "add", by: 1 }); return n; })()

test_cases.name: dispatch returns the action
test_cases.call: (() => { const counter = (state, action) => (action.type === "add" ? state + action.by : state); return createStore(counter, 0).dispatch({ type: "add", by: 1 }); })()

test_cases.name: works with object state
test_cases.call: (() => { const todos = (state, action) => (action.type === "add" ? { ...state, items: [...state.items, action.text] } : state); const store = createStore(todos, { items: [] }); store.dispatch({ type: "add", text: "a" }); store.dispatch({ type: "add", text: "b" }); return store.getState().items; })()
